name: [Part 1] Ordered values, duplicates, and shared cursor
[Part 1] Empty stream
[Part 2] Multiples start at the base
test:
s = MultiplesStream(3)
assert iter(s) is s
assert s.next() == 3
assert next(s) == 6
assert [s.next() for _ in range(4)] == [9, 12, 15, 18]

name: [Part 2] Independent streams, including base one
test:
a, b = MultiplesStream(1), MultiplesStream(4)
assert [a.next(), b.next(), a.next(), b.next(), b.next()] == [1, 4, 2, 8, 12]

name: [Part 3] Merge finite streams and preserve every duplicate
[Part 3] Finite stream plus infinite multiples
test:
s = MergeStream([OrderedIntStream([1, 4]), MultiplesStream(3)])
assert iter(s) is s
assert [next(s) for _ in range(7)] == [1, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 15]

name: [Part 3] Merge infinite streams with equal values
test:
s = MergeStream([MultiplesStream(2), MultiplesStream(3)])
assert [s.next() for _ in range(10)] == [2, 3, 4, 6, 6, 8, 9, 10, 12, 12]

name: [Part 3] Continue already consumed inputs
input: consume one value from each input before merging
test:
a, b = OrderedIntStream([1, 3, 8]), MultiplesStream(2)
assert a.next() == 1
assert b.next() == 2
s = MergeStream([a, b])
assert [s.next() for _ in range(6)] == [3, 4, 6, 8, 8, 10]

name: [Part 3] Read lazily through the supplied interface
input: custom streams with bounded lookahead; read five values
test:
class GuardedStream(Stream):
    def __init__(self, start, step):
        self.value = start
        self.step = step
        self.reads = 0

    def next(self):
        self.reads += 1
        assert self.reads <= 6, 'Do not materialize a source stream'
        value = self.value
        self.value += self.step
        return value

a, b = GuardedStream(0, 100), GuardedStream(1, 1)
s = MergeStream([a, b])
assert a.reads <= 1 and b.reads <= 1, 'At most one initial head per input'
for n in range(5):
    assert s.next() == n
    assert a.reads + b.reads <= n + 3, 'At most one upcoming value per input'
